newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Thursday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed amid uncertainty over market direction. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were narrowly mixed. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at a yield of 0.95/0.90 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 0.85/0.80 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.50/1.45 percent against 1.44/1.39 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.16/99.21 from Wednesday's close of S$99.15/99.20, September 2001 at S$97.36/97.41 versus S$97.37/97.42 and June 2003 at S$95.36/95.41 against S$95.37/95.42.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Wednesday's 3-1/8 3 percent.
